A tree had 1000 leaves before the onset of the dry season, when it sheds all its leaves. In the first week of the dry season, the tree shed 2/5 of the leaves. In the second week, it shed 40% of the remaining leaves.  In the third week, the tree shed 3/4 times as many leaves as it shed on the second week. Calculate the number of leaves the tree hadn't shed by the third week.

Given:
- Initial leaves: 1000
- First week: shed 2/5 of leaves
- Second week: shed 40% of remaining leaves
- Third week: shed 3/4 times as many leaves as the second week

First, calculate the leaves shed in the first week:
\[ \text{Leaves shed in first week} = \frac{2}{5} \times 1000 = 400 \]
Remaining leaves after first week:
\[ 1000 - 400 = 600 \]

Second week leaves shed:
\[ \text{Leaves shed in second week} = 40\% \times 600 = 0.4 \times 600 = 240 \]
Remaining leaves after second week:
\[ 600 - 240 = 360 \]

Third week leaves shed:
\[ \text{Leaves shed in third week} = \frac{3}{4} \times 240 = 180 \]
Remaining leaves after third week:
\[ 360 - 180 = 180 \]

FINAL: 180
